description: KUROX is a team of enthusiastic students passionate about space exploration, planetary science and technology. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to explore Earth locations that resemble lunar and Martian environments using open scientific datasets. We enjoy research, problem-solving, data analysis and building innovative solutions. We welcome collaborators interested in Python, web development, GIS, data visualization, astronomy and planetary science.
summary:
TerraLuna Atlas is an interactive platform designed to identify and compare Earth environments that share measurable characteristics with selected regions of the Moon and Mars. Our project addresses the challenge of finding terrestrial locations that can serve as analog environments for understanding planetary conditions and supporting future space exploration research.

Using open scientific datasets from NASA and other reliable sources, we aim to compare terrain features such as elevation, slope and surface ruggedness, along with environmental conditions and geological characteristics. The platform will present selected Earth locations alongside lunar and Martian reference regions through interactive maps, visual comparisons and evidence-based insights.

By bringing these datasets together in an accessible interface, TerraLuna Atlas aims to make planetary analog research easier to explore and understand. We also emphasize transparent data sources and scientific limitations so that similarities are interpreted responsibly rather than presented as proof of identical environments.
details:
TerraLuna Atlas – Earth-to-Moon & Mars Analog Discovery Platform

TerraLuna Atlas aims to develop an interactive platform that explores terrestrial environments with characteristics comparable to selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

The platform will bring together open scientific datasets from NASA and other reliable sources to compare Earth locations with planetary reference regions. It will focus on three major dimensions: terrain (elevation, slope and surface ruggedness), environmental conditions (such as surface temperature) and geological characteristics. Users will be able to explore selected locations through interactive maps, view comparative visualizations and understand the scientific evidence behind each comparison.

We plan to use Python for data processing and analysis, Streamlit for the user interface, Pandas and NumPy for dataset handling, and Plotly and mapping libraries for visualizations. Our project emphasizes transparent data sources, meaningful comparisons and clear communication of data limitations.

The creative aspect of TerraLuna Atlas is its combined exploration of Earth, lunar and Martian environments in one accessible platform. Rather than simply identifying similar-looking landscapes, it aims to support evidence-based comparisons that distinguish measured similarities from qualitative geological observations.

The project could help students, educators and space enthusiasts explore planetary science and understand how terrestrial analog environments can support research, technology testing and preparation for future space exploration missions.
